nbzinbreg

nbzinbreg fits negative binomial (NB) and zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression models for count data, with the estimation written from scratch. NB models are fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) alternated with Newton–Raphson for the dispersion parameter, and ZINB models by an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits. No general-purpose optimizer is used, and the results agree with MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl() well within the project’s tolerances.

Features

  • Two models. nbreg() for overdispersed counts and zinbreg() for counts with excess zeros, with a two-part formula y ~ x | z for the count and zero parts, offsets, weights, subset and na.action.
  • The usual methods. print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), logLik() (so AIC() and BIC() work), fitted(), residuals(), nobs() and predict(), including predicted means, zero probabilities and count probabilities, with standard errors.
  • Inference. Wald and profile-likelihood confidence intervals, likelihood-ratio tests of nested models with anova(), a test for overdispersion, and a boundary-aware bootstrap test of NB against ZINB.
  • Standard errors. An analytic Hessian of the ZINB log-likelihood (a numerical one is an option), and parametric bootstrap standard errors.
  • Diagnostics. Observed against expected count frequencies, hanging rootograms, simulation from a fitted model, and tidy() / glance() summaries.
  • Careful numerics. Step-halving and line searches, a mandatory check that EM never lowers the likelihood, a gradient check before declaring convergence, and informative errors for bad input.

Get started

  • Usage: a step-by-step guide with real output.
  • Reference: every function, grouped by task.
  • Report: the methods, the benchmarks against glm.nb() and zeroinfl(), a simulation study and an analysis of the NMES1988 data.

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("jaxsonbugg/nbzinbreg")

Quick start 

library(nbzinbreg)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit)
